title: Build settings

staticBuild.commandHelp: Runs in a sandboxed build container with your dependencies installed. Leave both fields empty to serve files already committed to the repository.
staticBuild.publishHelp: The folder the build writes, relative to the base directory, for example dist.
staticBuild.mismatch: Set both the build command and the publish directory, or clear both.

resolved.dockerfile: Builds {{dockerfile}} with {{where}} as the build context.
resolved.static: Serves a static site built from {{where}}.

pathHelp: Dockerfile paths are relative to the repository root, not to the base directory.

nudge.title: This looks like a monorepo. Pick a Dockerfile.
nudge.body: There is no app at the repository root, so auto-detect has nothing to build there and the next deploy will fail. Choose a Dockerfile from the repository.

form.dockerfileHelp: Relative to the repository root, for example apps/web/Dockerfile. Leave empty to use Dockerfile in the build context.
form.outputDirectoryHelp: The folder to serve, relative to the repository root.
form.baseDirectoryHelp: The folder used as the build context. Leave empty for the repository root. Keep the root when the Dockerfile copies files from several packages, for example with turbo prune.
form.invalidAbsolute: Use a path relative to the repository root, not an absolute path.
form.invalidParent: The path must stay inside the repository (no ..).
form.invalidOutside: The Dockerfile must be inside the base directory. Paths are relative to the repository root, for example {{example}}.

detected.title: Detected in this repo
detected.description: Dockerfiles and build roots found on branch {{branch}}.
detected.empty: No Dockerfiles or build roots were found on this branch.
detected.truncated: The repository is large, so this list may be incomplete.

reasons.turboPrune: It runs turbo prune, so keep the build context at the repository root.
reasons.rootCopy: It copies the whole repository and workspace files, so keep the build context at the repository root.
reasons.appDeployDir: It sits in the deploy folder of {{app}}, which usually builds from the repository root.
reasons.rootDockerfile: A Dockerfile at the repository root, built with the whole repository as context.
reasons.nestedDockerfile: A Dockerfile in {{directory}}, built from that directory.
reasons.appRailpack: {{directory}} looks like an application, auto-detected from that directory.

failureActions.matchedFixes: Fixes matched from the build log

fromCache.started: Deploy from the source cache started

workspace.title: Workspace packages
workspace.description: Each package can run as its own service. Using one sets its directory as the build root and limits pushes to the paths that change it.
workspace.checkTitle: Check what a change would redeploy
workspace.checkLabel: Changed files, one per line (list both names for a rename)

sourceFields.branchesFailed: {{message}}. You can still type a branch, tag, or commit manually below.
sourceFields.refWithPicker: Branch, tag, or commit (or pick above)
sourceFields.autoDetectHelp: Recommended. Detects Node, Go, and Java projects and builds them automatically, no Dockerfile needed.
sourceFields.dockerfileHelp: Builds from a Dockerfile in the repository.
sourceFields.staticHelp: Serves the checkout directly, no container.
sourceFields.imageHelp: Deploys an already-built image from a registry directly, no git repository or build step at all.
sourceFields.imageRefHelp: A full registry reference, already built and pushed elsewhere. Deployed as-is.
sourceFields.imageNameHelp: The name given to the built image. Leave blank to use the app name.
sourceFields.dockerfilePathHelp: Where the Dockerfile lives in your repo. Leave blank if it's at the root.
sourceFields.baseDirectoryHelp: Subdirectory to build from, for a monorepo. Leave blank to build from the repo root.
sourceFields.buildArgsHelp: Dockerfile ARG values passed to the build, for example a base image version or a build-time feature flag.

push.title: Deploy with git push
push.description: Beta. Push a branch to a remote on this server and it builds and deploys that exact commit. Clone and fetch are not supported.
push.off: Git push deploy is switched off. It is a beta feature and off by default.
push.notEnabled: Not enabled for this app. Enabling it creates a push token, shown once.
push.shownOnce: The token is shown once and stored only as a hash. Then deploy with: git push {{remote}} {{branch}}
push.copyCommand: Copy the git remote add command
push.copyRemote: Copy the git remote add line
push.credentials: When git asks for credentials, use the user name {{user}} and the push token as the password.
push.rotateBody: A new token is shown once. The current token stops working at once, so update the remote in every clone that pushes.
push.revokeTitle: Turn off git push for this app?
push.revokeBody: The push token stops working at once. Deploys from other sources are not affected.

ciGate.title: Wait for CI before deploying
ciGate.description: Hold a push deploy until the commit's checks pass. If a check fails or the wait times out, the deploy is skipped and the reason shows in webhook deliveries and deploy history.
ciGate.checksHelp: Leave empty to wait for every check on the commit. Add names such as build or test to wait only for those.
ciGate.saveFailed: Could not save the CI gate.
